positive.reasoning: Criterion A1 (traumatic event): MET — patient described experiencing events where they felt a genuine threat to safety. Criterion B1 (intrusive memories): MET — patient reported recurrent memories and feelings of distress as if reliving the event. Criterion B2 (flashbacks): MET — patient mentioned feeling as though the event is happening again, with physical reactions. Criterion B3 (distress from reminders): MET — patient experiences distress triggered by sounds or environments. Criterion C1 (avoidance of thoughts): MET — patient actively tries to avoid thinking about distressing memories. Criterion C2 (avoidance of reminders): MET — patient avoids crowded areas and conversations that remind them of the trauma. Criterion D1 (negative beliefs about self/others): MET — patient expressed feelings of worthlessness and hopelessness. Criterion D2 (self-blame): MET — patient reported feelings of guilt and self-blame regarding the trauma. Criterion D3 (negative emotional state): MET — patient described persistent feelings of fear and guilt. Criterion D4 (anhedonia): MET — patient noted a decrease in interest in previously enjoyed activities. Criterion D5 (detachment): MET — patient reported feeling detached from others. Criterion D6 (inability to experience positive emotions): MET — patient described fleeting moments of joy. Criterion E1 (irritability): MET — patient reported increased irritability and outbursts. Criterion E2 (recklessness): MET — patient mentioned engaging in reckless behaviors. Criterion E3 (hypervigilance): MET — patient described feeling more on edge. Criterion E4 (startle response): MET — patient reported being more easily startled. Criterion E5 (concentration difficulties): MET — patient noted difficulty concentrating. Criterion E6 (sleep disturbances): MET — patient reported trouble sleeping. Criterion F (duration): MET — symptoms have persisted for over a month since the traumatic event. Criterion G (functional impairment): MET — patient described significant distress and interference with daily functioning. Exclusion criteria: NOT MET — patient denied substance use or medical conditions that could explain symptoms. Total: 14 of 14 criteria met (threshold ≥ 1). Diagnosis: TRUE — full criteria for PTSD are met with significant functional impairment confirmed.
